fields.value: Replication Data for:  Job coaching for people with SMI

dsDescriptionValue.value:
These data originate from a study on people with severe mental illness (SMI) residing in supported housing settings, finding and maintaining paid or unpaid work. This study examined how professionals adjust job‑coaching trajectories to respond to clients’ specific needs. It aimed to clarify how these trajectories unfold in practice and under which conditions individuals with SMI in supported housing are able to engage in and sustain meaningful daily activities — including paid or unpaid work — as part of their recovery. A realist evaluation approach was applied to identify what works for whom and under which circumstances. Self‑Determination Theory provided the lens to examine the motivational processes that encourage clients to pursue and sustain paid or unpaid work.
Data is based on qualitative interview data from individuals with severe mental illness (SMI) and their job coaches (interviews took place in dyads). In addition, two mixed focus groups were conducted, involving job coaches and their supervisors providing broader professional perspectives on job‑coaching practices.

fields.value:
This dataset contains the topiclist used for the interviews as well as the codes derived from these interviews. These were used for refinement during the focus group interviews. Analysis took place accordingly. 

Due to the highly sensitive and potentially identifiable nature of these interviews, making the full transcripts publicly available would compromise participant privacy and violates the conditions approved by the institutional ethics committee. Therefore, the full transcripts cannot be shared publicly. Requests for access will be reviewed by a committee and accessibility of the data is assured, provided there is a lawful basis for sharing the data.
